title: Make with AI on My Cuff or Bag
sentence: Explore a source pattern on a cuff or bag, respond to the AI preview with a material action, then compare what changes.
rq: How do people maintain or revise their understandings of authenticity through interaction with AI and cultural heritage?
purpose: A explores how material actions and AI image responses affect a person’s understanding of authenticity. A named textile object supplies the source. The cuff or bag is one everyday way to encounter its patterns.
steps: Choose a source and item
Read the textile object’s information and select a detail. Choose a cuff or bag area, with a study item available.
Approve a small photograph
Place the chosen area in the fixed tabletop window. Check and approve the local photograph.
See AI’s first preview
AI combines the source detail and approved photograph to propose a digital pattern preview.
Make a physical response
Fold, flatten or reposition the material after seeing the preview. Approve another local photograph, or keep the current result.
Compare and explain
Compare the two actual previews. Point to a change and explain what it carries from the source or your own experience.
Reflect and keep the result
Discuss the clearly labelled future museum arrangement and keep a source-credited visual record.
ai: In the working concept, AI adapts a named source pattern to an approved local cuff or bag photograph. The person’s next fold or position change becomes the next input. The source, photograph and AI preview remain visible together.
noai: The concept includes a route using the source and local item without generation. The person can keep a plain source-labelled record. Round 1 separately permits skipping or discarding drafts under its submitted protocol.
theory: Relational authenticity asks how a connection becomes meaningful through objects, people, making and history. We follow the connections visitors themselves describe.
Looking alike and having a real link
A similar shape is one possible reason. A known maker, source or history gives another kind of link. The personal item and original work each retain their own materials and histories.

We examine whether a visitor can see how their material action affects AI, guide the next image and decide when the result no longer fits the source. Embodied generation already has published precedents.
future: Imagine a museum that shares a textile work as changing digital patterns for visitors’ own cuffs and bags. Its label says “Each version continues the original work”. Looking at your two previews, what would you keep, change or rename in that museum?
speculation: The two actual previews and the clearly fictional label make this future museum concrete. Visitors can discuss how personal use carries a source forward, what should remain recognisable and how the artist and source should be credited. Their own answer guides the discussion.
record: For a later working-prototype study, a proposed record could link the source, approved photographs, AI previews, physical adjustments and participant explanations. The collection method would be specified in that study’s protocol. Round 1 uses the smaller, separate data set described below.
analysis: The working-prototype research would follow how people connect their actions, AI responses, the source work and their own experience. Round 1 first gathers written authenticity reflections, optional captions and source/image choices.
value: The candidate contribution is an account of how visitors maintain or change their grounds for a connection to one named heritage object during material interaction with AI. The interaction technique has close precedents. A contribution would need evidence from the action sequence and the visitor’s reasons.
setup: One permitted source detail and fact card, a fixed camera, a small tabletop window, one screen and one image-conditioned generation service. Visitors choose a cuff or bag corner. A plain study cuff or bag panel provides an alternative. Begin with two deliberate captures.
broad: Offer seated access, a plain study item and a helper who follows the visitor’s directions. People can point, speak or select a prepared outline. Explain and record the chosen capture route. AI use remains a choice.
checkpoint: Use Round 1 feedback to refine the task, examples and research prompts. Later iterations can test the live action-and-response loop and choose a detailed study method.

title: One Object, Two Interpretations
sentence: Exchange interpretations of the same object across languages, clarify the meaning, and develop a postcard that carries the exchange forward.
rq: How do people express and negotiate their understanding of a shared heritage object through AI-mediated cross-cultural exchange?
purpose: B explores expression and negotiation across cultural perspectives. The shared object anchors the conversation. AI offers language and image assistance, while original messages, real replies and clarifications remain visible. A related postcard develops from the exchange.
steps: Share one named object
Use the same object image, selected detail and checked information. An approved cuff or bag photograph can provide a personal visual setting.
Express an interpretation
Write or say what the object means to you in your own language. Check the original words.
Develop and share a draft
AI assists with translation and a source-related image preview. Original words, labelled translation and source remain visible.
Receive a real response
Another person reads the source and interpretation, then replies, asks a question or offers a different reading.
Clarify and update
Keep the conversation visible. Clarify the words and, when useful, revise the associated image and postcard. Different interpretations can remain.
Keep a connected postcard
Choose the postcard linked to the exchange. The concept includes download or optional email delivery, with the delivery method to be specified for a later study.
ai: In the working concept, AI bridges languages and helps visualise an interpretation. It can assist a translation or image revision after a real response. People check their own expression and retain the original messages and conversation.
noai: Use direct language skills or study-team translation and a plain postcard showing the source, local-item reference and checked words. The real reply and clarification still develop that same card. Choose translation, image generation and delivery separately.
theory: Follow how the object, a person’s experience and the other visitor become connected through exchange.
Separate the sender’s endorsement of wording, the recipient’s understanding, historical accuracy and the recognition of an interpretation.

Being able to change a translation can help people express themselves. It can also make a conversation take more effort. AI writing suggestions may remove cultural details. These findings help us choose what to observe.
future: Imagine a future museum that shows the final AI-assisted postcards as visitors’ interpretations of an object. Which parts of your developing card should the next visitor see: the final version, the earlier draft and reply, or both?
speculation: Use the actual draft, real reply and final card beside a fictional future-display label. Participants decide how a museum should show a meaning that developed through conversation, and whose words or images should remain visible. The real source and each contributor remain identified.
record: A later working-prototype study could link original messages, translations, real replies, clarifications and related postcard versions. Approved local photographs and delivery choices would need their own specified handling. Round 1 collects the anonymous text and existing-image references listed in its protocol.
analysis: The working concept asks how meanings travel through expression, AI assistance, another person’s reply and clarification. Round 1 uses original messages, reply relationships, related postcards and questionnaire reflections to refine that activity.
value: The candidate contribution is an account of how a source-related personal meaning develops through a multilingual conversation around one AI-assisted visual postcard. Its draft and revision show how people recognise, question and clarify each other’s interpretations. The final card keeps the outcome of that same process.
setup: A shared digital source, a conversation interface, language and image assistance, a real reply channel and a linked postcard view. A local cuff/bag image can use the same small capture station as A. The implementation and delivery method will develop through later iterations.
broad: The concept supports different languages, individual participation, help with input and a plain-card route. Round 1 starts with adult ECS staff and students, using prepared content and a local whiteboard.
checkpoint: Use Round 1 to improve the conversation and postcard relationship. Later iterations can test live language and image assistance and specify the study procedure.
